narrative.en:
The mag-lift hums like a held breath as it climbs the AmourCorp tower.

Outside, Echocity blurs into a smear of light and rain, each floor you pass flashing a different fantasy: curated couples in champagne lounges, silhouettes pressed against tinted glass, private rooms where laughter has a price tag.

Your HUD tags it all:
> *ENGAGEMENT SCORE: 94*
> *SATISFACTION PREDICTED: 3–5 WEEKS.*

At floor 200, the doors slide open with a soft hydraulic sigh.

Calvin is waiting.

Black suit with a faint silver circuit tracery, collar undone just enough to be deliberate. His eyes catch the light the way expensive things do—subtle, engineered, dangerous.

His gaze travels over you, slow, like he's reading a graph.

> **Calvin:** "Not bad. I was curious what you'd look like outside baseline conditions."

He steps closer. You smell rain, synth-cologne, and something colder underneath—filtered air, server chill.

His fingers reach toward your collar, precise.

> **Calvin:** "You missed a crease. Can't bring you in wrinkled. People might think I'm slipping."

His hand hovers for a second, waiting to see if you'll let him touch you.

text.en: Let him fix your collar. Hold his gaze.
Step back slightly. Keep it professional.

narrative.en:
He adjusts your collar—his fingers careful, almost reverent, almost clinical. Then he steps back, satisfied.

> **Calvin:** "Come on. I want to show you what you've been working for without realizing it."

The gala unfolds like a simulation:

Floating holo-panels replay "successful match stories" over real bodies draped in designer fabric. Every guest is tagged in your vision with live metrics—**desirability**, **trend velocity**, **break-up likelihood**.

In the center of the room, a translucent model of a brain spins slowly, neural pathways glowing in neon blues and reds. Above it, a tagline:

> **HEARTLINE 3.0 – WE DON'T GUESS. WE KNOW.**

Calvin stands beside you, hands in his pockets, looking up at his own creation as if it's something intimate.

> **Calvin:** "This is the new feature. Predictive infidelity. Six months accuracy, 93% confidence. We sell peace of mind… and a reason to leave before they do."

The nearby execs murmur approval, champagne glasses chiming like a quiet ritual.

Calvin leans closer, lips near your ear, voice low enough to be almost a touch.

> **Calvin:** "Imagine owning the switch that decides who the city calls *faithful*… and who it quietly pushes toward the trash lane."

His breath warms the shell of your ear. On the screen, a demo couple laughs while a red bar above their heads flickers: *CHEATING RISK – 71%.*

text.en: "That's disgusting. Gaming people's hearts."
"Impressive. Dangerous. Kind of thrilling."
"What would you rate me?"

narrative.en:
Whatever you say, Calvin studies your face more than your words. The metrics dancing in your HUD have nothing on the way his gaze parses you.

> **Calvin:** "Come."

He touches a control on his cuff, and a section of mirrored wall irises open. The noise of the gala fades as you step into a narrow corridor of dark glass and soft light, the city dropping away beneath your feet.

In the air between you, your **AmourCorp profile** materializes—lines of text, charts, projections.

> **CALIBRATED ROLE:** Mid-tier analyst
> **POTENTIAL:** High, underleveraged
> **RISK:** *'Romantic tendencies. Susceptible to non-optimal attachments.'*

Calvin swipes through your life like it's a slide deck.

> **Calvin:** "You're efficient. Creative. Too honest. You still think love is some… organic phenomenon that happens between people, instead of a system we can optimize."

He flicks his fingers; your projected future arcs upward—more credits, more access, private floors.

> **Calvin:** "I can fix your trajectory. Title. Raise. Full access to restricted data. No more glass ceilings. Only glass floors."

The corridor's transparent floor brightens, revealing Echocity far below. One step forward would feel like falling.

His hand hovers in the space between you—too low for a handshake, too high for anything innocent.

> **Calvin:** "Say yes, and tonight is a beginning. Say no, and you can go back to watching from the ground, wondering what it feels like to actually matter."

text.en: "I'm done with illusions."
"My heart isn't part of your quarterly targets."
"What does 'alignment' look like after midnight?"

unavailable_text.en: Unlock 'Midnight Terms' to push past professional into something dangerous.

narrative.en:
He doesn't smile when you agree. He just nods, like a hypothesis has been confirmed.

Another door unlocks with a soft, heavy click. The room beyond is small and intimate: low light, deep grey walls, a couch that looks like it belongs in a therapist's office or a very discreet club.

The glass floor here is perfectly clear. The city spins lazily under your feet, as if you're standing on the surface of a lens.

A contract appears in the air between you, pages of dense legal text scrolling slowly.

You catch key phrases:

> *"Non-disclosure of internal affective experiments."*
> *"Priority access override to emotional telemetry streams."*
> *"Exclusive access during designated priority cycles."*

Your name appears, waiting for consent.

Calvin stands close enough that his presence feels like an extra layer of climate control.

> **Calvin:** "This is where you stop being just another employee."

He taps one clause, and the text glows.

> **Calvin:** "This line means I see what you feel. When you're in my building. When you're on my projects. Sometimes when you're thinking about me when you shouldn't be."

He looks at you, the faintest trace of amusement at the edge of his mouth.

> **Calvin:** "You can say no. Echocity is full of people who did. I just don't tend to remember their names."

text.en: Sign without asking questions.
Read every line. Ask about 'exclusive access'.
Sign the deeper override. Become his priority subject.

unavailable_text.en: Unlock 'Emotional Access Override' to sign the deeper terms.

text.en: "This is too invasive. I can't."

narrative.en:
The temperature in the room seems to drop three degrees.

Calvin adjusts his cufflink—a small, deliberate motion that somehow feels like a door closing.

> **Calvin:** "Idealistic."

He says it like he's diagnosing a minor defect in a prototype.

> **Calvin:** "Echocity eats idealists, {player_name}. Digests them slowly. Spits out middle managers with good intentions and no leverage."

He turns slightly, his profile sharp against the city lights.

> **Calvin:** "I thought you might be… adaptable. Someone who understood that the game is rigged and chose to rig it back."

His eyes return to you, recalculating.

> **Calvin:** "But maybe I misread. It happens. Rarely."

You can feel the opportunity contracting, the air growing thinner. He's giving you one more chance to change your answer—or confirm it.

text.en: "I'm not for sale. Not to you. Not to anyone."
"I just need time to think. This is a lot."

narrative.en:
You confirm the contract. A soft chime, a glow of your name, and somewhere deep in the tower, a system accepts that a part of you now belongs to the company—and to Calvin.

Your HUD flickers as new permissions cascade through your implants. Emotional telemetry. Priority channels. Restricted floors.

Calvin steps closer, into your newly signed space.

> **Calvin:** "Look up."

The glass wall darkens, then clears to a reflection—not of you, but of your metrics.

Heart rate, micro-expressions, arousal index, trust coefficients. All mapped in clean, elegant lines.

As he reaches toward you, the graphs twitch.

He brushes his thumb along your jaw, a touch light enough to deny if someone asked. Your data spikes.

> **Calvin:** "See? I haven't even done anything, and you're already reacting."

His tone is almost gentle. Almost.

> **Calvin:** "This is what I mean by potential. You don't hide. You don't flatten. You *feel*."

His thumb pauses at the corner of your mouth, then trails down your throat, stopping just above the pulse point your implant monitors.

> **Calvin:** "Most people in this tower are numbers pretending to be human. You're the opposite. I can work with that. Or break it. Depends on where you land."

Your reflection shows two figures: one composed, immaculate; the other raw, exposed in data.

text.en: Lean into his touch. Let him see everything.
Hold still. Try to keep your metrics flat.
"Do you prefer watching or causing?"

narrative.en:
You haven't fully surrendered. Calvin notices—and something shifts in his posture. Interest, maybe. Or the patience of a predator who enjoys the chase.

> **Calvin:** "You want terms. Fine. What are your conditions?"

You lay them out: your emotional data stays private outside work hours. No surveillance of who you see, who you touch, who you love. Your off-time remains yours.

He listens, head tilted, like you're speaking a quaint dialect.

> **Calvin:** "Reasonable. Naive, but reasonable."

He counters: he won't read everything—"only enough to avoid surprises." He'll know when you lie to him. He'll know when you think about him. But he won't share it.

> **Calvin:** "I'm not interested in owning you. That's boring. I'm interested in seeing what you choose when you know I'm watching."

The negotiation itself becomes a kind of dance—each boundary you draw is a line he wants to step over. Each concession feels like losing and winning at once.

> **Calvin:** "You negotiate like someone who's been burned before. Good. Scars make people careful. Careful people are useful."

text.en: "Hard lines. Non-negotiable. Take it or leave it."
"Partial access. That's my limit."

narrative.en:
When you return to the gala, everything feels louder.

Music pulses through the floor, synced with the slow thud of your own heartbeat in the HUD. More guests have arrived—polished, laughing, masked. A low buzz follows you, subtle glances pinging off Calvin and landing on you, recalibrating their assumptions.

His hand finds the small of your back. Barely there. Possessive in a way only people on this floor are trained to notice.

Your profile pings:

> *VISIBILITY SCORE: +230%*
> *PERCEIVED VALUE: UPGRADED*

On the largest screen, anonymous live Heartline feeds flicker: fragmentary glimpses of strangers in various states of intimacy, despair, ecstasy. Emotions captured, anonymized, looped as entertainment.

> **Calvin:** "Transparency. It makes people behave."

You watch a clip of someone crying alone on a balcony, AR lenses still on, scrolling for validation. Another of two bodies tangled together, faces blurred, metrics sharp.

You suddenly feel very aware that if Calvin wanted, you could be up there too—your data, not your face. Your reactions to his touch, charted and sold as "engagement."

Behind you, a man in a mirrored mask leans in to another exec and whispers just loud enough:

> **Exec:** "So this is Calvin's new project. Pretty."

You feel Calvin's fingertips press slightly into your back, a tiny increase in pressure as he waits to see what you'll do.

text.en: Play along. Smile like you belong on his arm.
Pull away. Put distance between you.
Quietly: "I'm not a product, Calvin."

narrative.en:
Later, the noise and light fall away.

Calvin leads you out a side door and up a short flight of metal steps. A blast of cooler air hits your skin as you step onto the rooftop helipad.

Echocity spreads out in all directions, a living circuit board. Drones trace soft arcs between towers. The rain has thinned to a fine mist that makes every light halo.

Up here, the music is a low throb through the concrete. The rest is silence.

Calvin stands near the edge, hands in his pockets, watching the city like it's a dashboard.

> **Calvin:** "This is the real product, you know."

He gestures at the sprawl.

> **Calvin:** "Millions of people, all convinced they're making free choices. All we do is tilt the floor a little. They roll where we want."

He turns to you, expression unreadable but intent.

> **Calvin:** "Tonight was a test. Not for you. For me. To see whether investing in you is smart."

He takes a step closer. Up here, there are no reflections, no graphs—just the two of you and the drop.

> **Calvin:** "So. Tell me the truth."

His gaze pins you.

> **Calvin:** "Are you here because you want the life I can give you… or because you want *me*?"

If you signed the contract, your HUD quietly notes: *EMOTIONAL STREAM ACTIVE.* You know he'll see whatever this answer does to you.

text.en: "Both. The life and you."
"I'm here for my career. Only."
"I don't know. And I don't trust you."

narrative.en:
The words leave your mouth and hang there between you and the city.

You want his world.
You want him in it.

For a second, Calvin just looks at you—as if you were a number on a screen that suddenly refused to stay in its column.

Then, slowly, he smiles. It's not the polished, public smile from the gala. It's smaller. Sharper. Private.

> **Calvin:** "Good."

He steps closer. The mist clings to his hair, his shoulders, the open edge of his collar. Under the city's glow, he looks like an ad for something you can't afford and already bought.

> **Calvin:** "Clarity is rare up here. Most people lie to me first, then to themselves."

He studies your face like a problem worth solving.

> **Calvin:** "You—"

His gaze drops to your lips, then lower, tracking micro-twitches your implants can't hide.

> **Calvin:** "You're honest enough to know this is a terrible idea. And you still stepped into the elevator."

A breeze sweeps across the rooftop, tugging at your clothes. The drop at your back feels closer, the sky heavier.

He lifts a hand and traces the line of your throat with his knuckles, slow, almost absentmindedly, as if mapping access points.

> **Calvin:** "So we don't pretend. You want the life. You want me. I want to see what you become when you stop holding back."

His fingers stop at your wrist-implant, pressing lightly over the interface.

> **Calvin:** "The only question is whether you survive the upgrade."

The city hums beneath you, like an audience waiting for your next move.

text.en: Take the initiative. Close the distance between you.
Stay still. Let him decide what happens next.
Step back. Say you won't be the one he tests his theories on.

narrative.en:
Your answer is clean. Surgical.

You're here for the life. Not for him.

The words put a faint crack in the mood. Calvin hears it. Of course he does.

For a heartbeat, something unreadable flickers across his face—disappointment or admiration or nothing at all. Then it's gone, neatly archived.

He takes a small step back, enough to replace heat with air.

> **Calvin:** "Efficient. I appreciate that."

His tone sharpens into the one you've heard in boardrooms and internal calls, the voice that moves whole departments like pawns.

> **Calvin:** "Then let's not romanticize this. I'll use your talents. You'll use my access. We'll both pretend it's not exploitation because the numbers balance."

He extends his hand, palm up—too formal for the rooftop, too intimate for a contract. A gesture that says: *we are not lovers; we are a deal.*

The city glows below, waiting to see which side of yourself you feed.

text.en: Shake his hand. Accept the purely transactional arrangement.
Refuse. Say you're not willing to be 'used,' even for the top floor.

narrative.en:
The silence after your answer is heavier than the air.

You don't dress it up. You don't soften it. You just lay the truth between you like a piece of broken glass: you don't know what you want from him yet—and you don't trust him.

For a long second, Calvin doesn't move. The city roars below, all soft static from this height.

Then, unexpectedly, he laughs. Not mockingly—more like someone hearing a rare sound.

> **Calvin:** "Interesting."

He steps closer again, but not as near as before. You feel the boundary you set, and so does he.

> **Calvin:** "Most people on this roof would have lied. Told me whatever they thought would get them the keys."

He studies you with something that might almost be respect.

> **Calvin:** "You'd risk offending me rather than give me a clean datapoint. That's either very brave or very stupid."

His gaze drifts past you, to the drop, then back.

> **Calvin:** "Trust is… inefficient in Echocity. But I find myself curious what you look like when you give it to someone. If you ever do."

He lets the question hang there, not demanding an answer.

> **Calvin:** "For now, we'll call this… a provisional arrangement. I won't ask you for loyalty you don't feel. You don't pretend I'm anything but dangerous."

His mouth tilts slightly.

> **Calvin:** "We'll see who changes first."

The rotor lights flicker on around the helipad, casting the two of you in a ghostly circle of white.

text.en: Tell him if he wants you loyal, he'll have to earn it.
Apologize. Say you're just overwhelmed and didn't mean to push him away.

narrative.en:
The next cycle begins with the soft chime of your implant and a headache made of neon and bad decisions.

Your capsule apartment is exactly where you left it: too small, too clean, full of cheap surfaces pretending to be more than they are. Your clothes smell faintly of rain and filtered air, not the undercity.

Your HUD boots fully.

New notifications burst across your vision:

> **AMOURCORP INTERNAL:** *Role updated – Access Level ↑*
> **CREDITS:** *Performance bonus applied*
> **PERMISSIONS:** *Restricted floors unlocked (Tiers 2–4)*

A new icon throbs in the corner of your interface: **CALVIN – PRIORITY CHANNEL**.

You expand it.

A log appears—not of messages, but of **data access**:

> *Emotional stream access: 4 hours 13 minutes*
> *Location: AmourCorp Tower – Private Floors*
> *Subject: [YOUR NAME]*
> *Authorization: Executive Override – C. [REDACTED]*

You flick through fragments of memory: the rooftop, the contracts, the way the city looked when you almost forgot where you ended and his world began.

Another notification lands, crisp and simple—a message from Calvin.

> **Calvin:** "You adapted quickly. The metrics were… promising."

A pause, then another line appears.

> **Calvin:** "Don't make me regret this."

No emoji. No softness. Just the subtle weight of someone who now knows exactly how your nervous system sings when he steps too close.

Outside, the rain has stopped. Echocity glows, waiting to see what you'll do with what you just sold.

text.en: Feel exhilarated. This is the life you wanted.
Feel used. Something in you feels… sold.

narrative.en:
Later, in the half-light between notifications and sleep, your implant compiles a quiet summary:

> **CHAPTER 1: GLASS TOWERS – PERSONAL REPORT**

Lines of data arrange themselves into something that looks uncomfortably like a confession.

- **Love Integrity:** {{love_integrity_value}}
- **Temptation Index:** {{temptation_value}}
- **Career Status:** {{career_status_value}}

Underneath, the system annotates your night in cool, neutral language:

- *You walked into AmourCorp's highest floors and stayed.*
- *You [SIGNED / REFUSED] Calvin's contract.*
- *You [ALLOWED / DENIED] emotional access overrides.*
- *You treated Calvin as [AN INVESTMENT / A DANGER / BOTH].*

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Echocity doesn't remember the people who stayed on the ground.

Tonight, you stepped onto the glass—with Calvin's hand on your back and the city below, ready to watch you rise or shatter.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

A faint system note appears:

> Somewhere in the tower, Calvin flags your profile: *"Do not discard."*

The report fades, replaced by a simple prompt:

> **Echocity waits. Calvin is watching.**
> What you do next decides whether you become his greatest success story… or his favorite mistake.

text.en: Continue: Chapter 2 – Corporate Experiments
Ghost the tower for a night. Answer Jackson's late-night ping.
Dive offline. Follow Cole's encrypted trail.

narrative.en:
The question hangs in the air like smoke.

*What does 'alignment' look like after midnight?*

Calvin's expression shifts—something predatory surfaces beneath the polished exterior. He doesn't answer immediately. Instead, he steps closer, close enough that you can smell the filtered tower air clinging to his collar.

> **Calvin:** "Curious."

He reaches past you, and the corridor dims. The city lights below become the only illumination, casting both of you in blue and gold shadows.

> **Calvin:** "Most people ask about salary. Benefits. Vacation days."

His fingers find your chin, tilting your face up. His touch is cool, precise—like he's adjusting a display.

> **Calvin:** "You ask about midnight."

The contract hovers forgotten in the air beside you. This isn't in any clause.

> **Calvin:** "Alignment after midnight means I stop treating you like an investment and start treating you like... an interest."

His thumb traces your jawline, stopping just below your ear where your implant pulses.

> **Calvin:** "It means I see what makes you respond. What makes you forget to breathe. What makes your metrics do things the algorithm can't predict."

He leans closer, lips almost brushing yours.

> **Calvin:** "It means you become someone I think about when I shouldn't. And you let me."

The city spins beneath the glass floor. Your heart rate spikes—and he watches it happen in real-time, a faint smile curving his mouth.

> **Calvin:** "So. Still want to know what alignment looks like?"

His other hand finds the small of your back, pulling you closer to the edge of professional and something far more dangerous.

text.en: Close the distance. Show him exactly what you want.
"Show me. But I set the pace."
"That's... a lot. Maybe we should focus on the contract."

narrative.en:
**Chapter 2: Corporate Experiments**

Calvin has plans for you. Projects that blur the line between employee and subject. Nights that blur the line between power and intimacy.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

> What you've seen so far is just the onboarding.
> Calvin hasn't even started the real experiments.
>
> Unlock **Glass Towers: Extended Route** to:
> - Enter the internal labs where Heartline is rewritten,
> - Face competitors who'd like to erase you,
> - Discover exactly what Calvin does to people he can't control.

text.en: Unlock Glass Towers: Extended Route

unavailable_text.en: Requires Glass Towers: Extended Route pack

text.en: Ghost the tower. Answer Jackson's ping instead.
Wait for now...

narrative.en:
The elevator doesn't have a floor number this time.

Your implant only shows a single word as you descend:

> **ACCESS: RESTRICTED**

The doors open to a corridor that feels nothing like the gala. No music. No glass floors. Just smooth white walls that swallow sound and a temperature set a few degrees too cold.

Calvin is waiting for you again. No suit jacket tonight—just a dark shirt, sleeves rolled to the forearms, throat bare. Less "executive ad" and more "surgeon between operations."

> **Calvin:** "You're on time."

His tone makes it sound like a test you've barely passed.

He walks with you down the corridor. Through a windowed wall, you see them:

Rows of reclined chairs—pods without lids. People lie there in neutral grey clothing, wired at the temples and wrists. Their faces twitch in micro-expressions: pleasure, panic, relief, confusion. Above each chair, a cluster of graphs pulses.

Your HUD tags them automatically:

> *SUBJECT – BETA COHORT*
> *REAL-TIME AFFECTIVE STREAM: ACTIVE*
> *INFORMED CONSENT: [REDACTED]*

Calvin watches you watching them.

> **Calvin:** "Welcome to the lab. This is where we stop pretending love is random."

He gestures at the monitors flooding the far wall. Every emotion is a number here. Every number has a price.

> **Calvin:** "Heartline 3.0 was just the prototype. The Board wants something bolder. A system that doesn't just predict who cheats… it decides who gets access to real relationships in the first place."

He glances sideways at you.

> **Calvin:** "You said you were done with illusions. Ready to matter."

A beat.

> **Calvin:** "This is what 'mattering' looks like."

He stops by a viewing station. Below, one of the subjects laughs in an empty, looped way, eyes closed, fingers clutching at nothing.

> **Calvin:** "Before we go further I need to know something."

He turns fully toward you now, no screens between you, just the low hum of machines.

> **Calvin:** "When I ask you to help calibrate this system… are you going to give me clean data? Or are you going to start protecting people who look too much like you?"

His gaze doesn't waver.

> **Calvin:** "Think carefully before you answer. The model isn't the only thing being tested tonight."

text.en: "I'll give you clean data. No protection, no illusions."
"If something feels wrong, I won't lie for you or the model."
"I don't know yet. Maybe that's why you brought me."

narrative.en:
Calvin studies your answer like it's a data point—which, to him, it probably is.

> **Calvin:** "We'll see."

He leads you deeper into the facility, through doors that open only for his biometrics. The hum of machinery grows louder, more present.

> **Calvin:** "Tonight's test is simple. Single subject. Controlled environment. You'll enter a simulation and respond naturally to prompts."

He hands you a thin neural interface disc.

> **Calvin:** "The system reads your reactions, cross-references them with the subject's profile, and adjusts the model accordingly. You're not just taking a test—you're helping write the algorithm that decides who deserves love in Echocity."

His lips curve into something that's almost a smile.

> **Calvin:** "No pressure."

text.en: "Let's do this."
"What happens to the subjects who fail?"

narrative.en:
The simulation room is smaller than you expected. No high ceilings, no dramatic glass—just a circular space with a single chair in the center and a ring of dim projectors hanging like a halo.

Calvin stands by the door, tablet in hand.

> **Calvin:** "We're starting easy. Single subject. Controlled environment."

He motions to the chair.

> **Calvin:** "Sit. The system will feed you a live interaction. All you have to do is respond naturally. We'll handle the rest."

You sit. The chair conforms to your shape in a way that feels a little too eager. Cold sensors kiss the back of your neck.

The lights dim. The world tilts.

When it settles, you're no longer in the lab.

You're in a modest apartment, the kind people in mid-levels still think is "cozy." On the couch in front of you sits a person—late twenties, eyes tired in a familiar way. A half-finished drink on the table. Heartline glow faint around their wrist.

Your HUD tags them:

> *SUBJECT #34 – STATUS: PILOT COHORT*
> *RELATIONSHIP HISTORY: 3 LONG-TERM, 4 SHORT-TERM*
> *LOYALTY SCORE (BETA): 42% – HIGH DEFECTION RISK*

Subject #34 looks up at you with a wry little smile, as if you just walked in the door.

> **Subject #34:** "You're late."

Their voice is warm, worn at the edges.

> **Subject #34:** "Heartline keep you busy?"

There's a familiarity to the script that worms under your skin. It's the echo of old arguments, old apologies. The shape of an ex, or a version of yourself you hate.

> **System (in your HUD):**
> *Test Prompt: Simulated partner scenario. Evaluate trust/attachment potential.*

You feel Calvin's presence like a cold hand at the back of your neck—he's watching your biometric patterns, even if he's not in the room.

The subject leans back, studying you.

> **Subject #34:** "Be honest with me for once. Do you think people can actually stay loyal in a city like this? Or are we all just… killing time until a better offer blinks in our feed?"

text.en: "Loyalty's real. People just use the system as an excuse to bail."
"No. Loyalty's a sales pitch. Everyone's scrolling for something better."
"I think we want to be loyal. I just don't think the city lets us."

narrative.en:
Subject #34 watches your face like they can see the weight behind your answer, even though they're just an instance in a test.

> **Subject #34:** "You sound like you've done this before. The speech. The justification."

A soft laugh.

> **Subject #34:** "So what about you? If I let you in—really in—are you the one who stays… or the one who walks when the metrics dip?"

The HUD flashes:

> *Secondary Prompt: Self-projection index. Do not overthink.*

You feel the urge to look for Calvin, to see if he's judging your answer, but the sim gives you nothing. Just the subject's eyes, waiting.

text.en: "I stay. Even when it stops being easy."
"I walk when it stops feeling good."
"I don't know. Depends who I'm with."

narrative.en:
The apartment glitches. For a split second, Subject #34's face dissolves into raw data—formulas, tags, a short note:

> *PSYCH PROFILE: RESEMBLANCE TO [YOUR NAME]: 71%*

Then the sim cuts. You're back in the small room. Lights up.

Calvin is there, tablet in hand, attention fixed entirely on you.

> **Calvin:** "Loyalty at the edges. Cynicism in the center. Self-doubt threaded throughout."

He doesn't specify whether he means **Subject #34** or **you**.

Your implant pings a silent result:

> *MODEL ADJUSTMENT: 0.7%*
> *INFLUENCE: SIGNIFICANT*

Calvin steps closer, just enough to make the air feel thinner.

> **Calvin:** "The model agrees with you. Subject #34 is… unreliable. Not worth routing into premium matches."

A beat.

> **Calvin:** "You just helped close a door on someone's version of a happy ending. Efficient, isn't it?"

There's no accusation in his tone. There doesn't need to be. The numbers did it for him.

text.en: "If they're that unstable, maybe it's better this way."
"We just declared someone unworthy based on a thirty-second sim."
"How many people did you do this to before me?"

narrative.en:
Calvin absorbs your reaction the way he absorbs everything—filing it, weighing it, deciding what it means for his models.

> **Calvin:** "You're processing. Good. That means it landed."

He sets down the tablet and walks toward you, hands in his pockets, posture deceptively casual.

> **Calvin:** "The Board thinks this is about efficiency. Matching the 'right' people, filtering out the 'wrong' ones. But you and I both know what this really is."

He stops close enough that you can see the faint pulse at his throat.

> **Calvin:** "Control. Pure, elegant control over the messiest thing humans do."

His eyes find yours.

> **Calvin:** "The question is: do you want to help me perfect it… or do you want to pretend you're above it while benefiting from every door it opens?"

The lab hums around you. Somewhere, another subject laughs in their sleep, chasing a feeling that was engineered for them.

> **Calvin:** "We'll continue tomorrow. Get some rest."

He turns to leave, then pauses.

> **Calvin:** "And {player_name}? Don't think I didn't notice how your heart rate spiked when Subject #34 asked if you'd stay. The algorithm noticed too."

A thin smile.

> **Calvin:** "Goodnight."

text.en: Continue...

narrative.en:
🚧 **Chapter 2 continues...**

The lab tests have only begun. Calvin has more experiments planned—and more ways to blur the line between subject and collaborator.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Calvin's office is all clean lines and silent glass. The city lies beneath like a hologram he can resize at will.

You're halfway through a debrief on Subject #34 when he stops mid-sentence, eyes unfocusing for a fraction of a second.

Your implant buzzes in sympathy.

> **Calvin:** "You went off-grid last cycle."

He doesn't raise his voice. He doesn't need to.

> **Calvin:** "Your location logs show a gap around Level -22. No authorized assignments there. Emotional telemetry went patchy."

He turns his chair to face you fully.

> **Calvin:** "Explain."

text.en: "I needed air. The tower was... too much."
"Personal errand. Nothing that touches your metrics."
"I went to the Verge. With Jackson."

narrative.en:
Calvin's gaze cools by a few degrees.

> **Calvin:** "You're not a very good liar."

He taps his cuff; a faint map appears, showing a blurred smear of your whereabouts.

> **Calvin:** "The overlay says undercity. The emotional spikes say adrenaline and... something else."

He studies you the way he studies test subjects—looking for the data under the surface.

> **Calvin:** "I don't need you to confess. I just need you to understand that I know."

His fingers drum once against the desk.

> **Calvin:** "The Verge is... messy. Full of people who think chaos is freedom. But chaos doesn't build anything. It just consumes."

He leans back, expression unreadable.

> **Calvin:** "Whatever you're looking for down there, ask yourself: is it worth what you'd lose up here?"

text.en: "Maybe I'm just trying to figure out who I am outside your metrics."
"It won't happen again."

narrative.en:
The name lands in the room like a dropped blade.

Calvin leans back, considering.

> **Calvin:** "The fixer. Information broker. Criminal."

His mouth twists, not quite a smile.

> **Calvin:** "You run the tower by day and the Verge by night. Ambitious."

He stands, walking to the window. The city sprawls beneath him.

> **Calvin:** "People Jackson touches tend to fall. Not always immediately. But gravity is patient."

He turns back to you.

> **Calvin:** "I'm not going to forbid you from seeing him. That would be... inefficient. And you'd resent me."

A thin smile.

> **Calvin:** "But I am going to remember this conversation. And so will the system."

Your HUD flickers:

> *EMPLOYEE RISK INDEX: ELEVATED*
> *RECOMMENDATION: INCREASED MONITORING*

> **Calvin:** "Your choice. Just make sure you can live with both worlds knowing who you really are."

text.en: "I can handle the consequences."
"You don't get to control who I see outside work."

narrative.en:
The lab lights fade behind you. Calvin walks beside you down a quieter corridor, hands in his pockets, expression unreadable.

For once, there's no one watching—no glass, no Board logos, no test subjects. Just the two of you and the low hum of unseen machines.

> **Calvin:** "You're adapting."

It's not clear if that's a compliment or a warning.

> **Calvin:** "Most people flinch the first time they realize how much of themselves is archived here. You seemed... fascinated."

He studies your profile for a moment.

> **Calvin:** "Or was that just shock wearing a different mask?"

text.en: "It scared me. I just didn't want to show it in front of the Board."
"It fascinated me. Terrifies me too—but that doesn't make it less interesting."
"You didn't hire me to flinch."

narrative.en:
Calvin processes your answer, filing it somewhere behind those calculating eyes.

The corridor opens into a small observation deck—a private space with a view of the labs below. Test subjects move through their routines, unaware of being watched.

> **Calvin:** "Everyone who works here has a moment where they realize what we actually do. Not the marketing version. The real thing."

He stands at the railing, watching the subjects.

> **Calvin:** "Some quit. Some pretend they didn't see. Some..."

He glances at you.

> **Calvin:** "Some lean in. Decide that understanding the machine is better than being ground up by it."

The lights below shift, casting his face in alternating shadow and glow.

> **Calvin:** "Which one are you going to be?"

It's not a test. Or maybe it is. With Calvin, the line is always blurred.

text.en: "I'd rather understand than be understood."
"I'm still deciding. Ask me again when I've seen more."
"Maybe there's a third option you haven't considered."
